blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
At senior level, freight and carrier management is a discipline, not a procurement cycle. Carriers must be managed like suppliers of critical capacity — with multi-year relationships, transparent scorecards, joint planning for peak periods, and honest conversations about where each side is struggling. The team that treats carriers as interchangeable finds, eventually, that its best carriers are interchangeable too — and quietly drift to customers who respect them more.

The senior leader's work focuses on three things. Concentration: how much of our freight depends on any single carrier, and is that consistent with our risk tolerance? Relationship health: are our core carriers calling us first with problems, or last? And cost intelligence: do we know what we are actually paying per lane, per mode, per region, accurately enough to decide?

Freight management done well is mostly invisible. It shows up not in heroic negotiations but in the quiet fact that, year after year, the core carriers still return the call.

items.q: According to the text, how should carriers be managed?
options: As suppliers of critical capacity, over multi-year relationships
As a once-a-year procurement exercise
As interchangeable vendors won on price
As a purely administrative booking function
items.why: "Carriers must be managed like suppliers of critical capacity — with multi-year relationships…"

items.q: Which three areas does the senior leader's work focus on?
options: Price, volume and delivery speed
Concentration, relationship health and cost intelligence
Lanes, modes and warehouses
Contracts, penalties and compliance
items.why: "three things. Concentration… Relationship health… And cost intelligence."

items.q: What does the text imply happens to a firm that treats carriers as interchangeable?
options: It gains leverage in every negotiation
It secures the lowest rates in the market
It loses its best carriers to customers who respect them more
It simplifies its logistics footprint
items.why: Inferência: "its best carriers are interchangeable too — and quietly drift to customers who respect them more."

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with which statement?
options: A hard-won negotiation is the truest proof of freight excellence
Carrier concentration should be weighed against risk tolerance
Good freight management rarely announces itself
The best carriers can be lost as easily as any supplier
items.why: Inferência: o texto diz que a gestão bem feita é "mostly invisible" e aparece "not in heroic negotiations" — logo, a negociação heroica não é a prova.

items.q: What does "the core carriers still return the call" suggest?
options: That the firm has automated its communications
That carriers are contractually obliged to respond
That the relationship remains healthy enough that carriers still prioritise the firm
That negotiations have finally concluded
items.why: Inferência: retornar a ligação, ano após ano, é o sinal silencioso de que a relação (relationship health) continua boa.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Harry explicando ao novo CFO. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Welcome aboard. Before you sign anything, let me walk you through what last year's freight RFP actually bought us — and what it quietly cost.

On paper it looked disciplined. We put every lane out to tender, we squeezed the rates hard, and we booked the savings. The board was delighted. But two of our strongest carriers read that process for what it was: a message that they were interchangeable. They didn't argue. They simply reallocated their best capacity to shippers who treat them as partners.

So this quarter, when the port congestion hit, those two carriers returned everyone's call before ours. We paid spot rates that erased the entire saving — and then some. The number the RFP delivered was never the real number, because the cost of a damaged relationship doesn't show up on the rate card.

What I'd ask of you is this. Judge freight not by the headline rate but by three things: how concentrated we are on any single carrier, whether our core carriers still call us first, and whether we genuinely know what we pay per lane. Those are quieter metrics — but they're the ones that hold when the market turns.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: Why does Harry say last year's RFP "quietly cost" the firm?
options: It took too long to complete
It signalled to strong carriers that they were interchangeable
It breached a regulatory requirement
It exceeded the procurement budget
items.why: "two of our strongest carriers read that process for what it was: a message that they were interchangeable."

items.q: What did the two strong carriers do in response to the RFP?
options: They reallocated their best capacity to other shippers
They filed a formal complaint
They demanded higher rates upfront
They terminated their contracts immediately
items.why: "They simply reallocated their best capacity to shippers who treat them as partners."

items.q: What happened when port congestion hit this quarter?
options: The firm paid spot rates that erased the savings and more
The board approved a new RFP
The core carriers offered a discount
The firm switched to rail to avoid delays
items.why: "We paid spot rates that erased the entire saving — and then some."

items.q: What does Harry mean by "the number the RFP delivered was never the real number"?
options: The finance team miscalculated the savings
The RFP figures were deliberately falsified
The headline saving ignored the hidden cost of a damaged relationship
The rate card excluded taxes and surcharges
items.why: Inferência: "the cost of a damaged relationship doesn't show up on the rate card" — a economia declarada não capturava o custo real.

items.q: How would you best describe Harry's advice to the new CFO?
options: Rerun the RFP with tougher terms
Look past the headline rate to quieter, relationship-based metrics
Reject all savings targets on principle
Consolidate all freight onto a single carrier
items.why: Inferência: ele pede julgar por concentração, saúde da relação e inteligência de custo — "quieter metrics… that hold when the market turns."

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "We run this as a strategic discipline, not a mere procurement cycle." A procurement cycle is…
options: the recurring process of sourcing and buying goods or services
a carrier's delivery schedule
a long-term partnership agreement
an internal audit of supplier invoices
items.why: Procurement cycle = ciclo de compras: o processo recorrente de sourcing e aquisição.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "During peak season, we protect our access to freight ___ by planning jointly with carriers months in advance."
options: scorecard
capacity
concentration
tolerance
items.why: Capacity = capacidade: o espaço/recurso de transporte que precisamos garantir.

items.q: "Each carrier is reviewed against a quarterly scorecard." A scorecard here is…
options: a summary of that quarter's invoices
a legal record of contract breaches
a ranked list of the cheapest carriers
a structured measure of performance across several criteria
items.why: Scorecard = cartão de desempenho: mede reliability, risco e custo, não só preço.

items.q: "Before we allocate volume, we agree our risk tolerance." Risk tolerance means…
options: the penalty clause in the contract
the maximum discount we will accept
how much exposure or downside we are willing to accept
the carrier's insurance coverage
items.why: Risk tolerance = tolerância ao risco: quanto de exposição/downside estamos dispostos a aceitar.

items.q: Choose the correct phrase: "Without proper ___, we can't say what we truly pay per lane, per mode, per region."
options: relationship health
risk tolerance
joint planning
cost intelligence
items.why: Cost intelligence = inteligência de custo: saber, com precisão, onde cada centavo é gasto.

blocks.instruction: Expressões e phrasal verbs que aparecem em reuniões de logística e negociação. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The CFO still has to sign off on the new carrier framework." To sign off on means to…
options: formally approve
postpone indefinitely
renegotiate
comment informally
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "We plan to roll out the scorecard model across all regions next year." To roll out means to…
options: explain it to the board only
quietly cancel it
test it in secret
implement it in stages
items.why: Roll out = implementar de forma progressiva, região por região.

items.q: "Two carriers pushed back on the aggressive rate terms." They…
options: forwarded them to legal
resisted or objected to them
signed them immediately
accepted them without comment
items.why: Push back on = resistir, discordar — sem necessariamente romper de vez.

items.q: "We agreed to joint planning last spring, but nobody followed through." They…
options: delegated it to the carrier
documented it thoroughly
revised the timeline
failed to carry it to completion
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim aquilo que foi combinado.

items.q: "Shaving another two percent off the rate won't move the needle on our capacity risk." This means it will…
options: provoke the carriers
increase costs sharply
take months to measure
make no meaningful difference
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, fazer diferença perceptível.
